title: (No AI) Anthropic clamps down on Claude’s AI video game clones
author: Jay Peters
content:
![Anthropic logo on an orange and gray background.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/01/STK269_ANTHROPIC_2_B.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Anthropic has updated Claude Code's system prompt to prevent the AI tool from being used to re-create existing video games, [as reported by _Tom's Hardware_](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/artificial-intelligence/anthropic-confirms-new-claude-code-limits-to-prevent-game-cloning-users-report-opus-5-5-is-also-actively-blocking-reverse-engineering-tasks). Retro gaming is currently being overrun [with AI-made decompilations, recompilations, and ports](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1015430/ai-retro-games-decomp-recomp-port), but while Anthropic will still let people use Claude Code to make games, it doesn't want people to use it for direct clones.

Last week, a user on X [posted a screenshot](https://x.com/chasmmmmmmmmmmm/status/2116062991686721968) allegedly showing two new sentences added to Claude Code's system prompt: "Do build original games, games in a genre, and games from the user's own designs and assets. Don't build a recreation of a specific existing game, even if …

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1024632/anthropic-claude-ai-video-game-clones)

title: (No AI) OpenAI pitches data center power plants as a way to protect nearby areas
author: Emma Roth
content:
![Chat GPT logo on a graphic green background.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/08/STK155_OPEN_AI_4_CVirginia_A.png?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

In [an announcement on Monday](https://openai.com/index/grid-protectors-program/), OpenAI says it will pilot its "Grid Protectors Program" at an upcoming data center in Effingham County, Georgia, where the company promises to free up to 1,000 megawatts of power during extreme weather or emergencies, enough to power air conditioners in around 700,000 homes.

The announcement comes as [opposition to data centers](https://www.theverge.com/policy/1019152/data-centers-midterm-elections) spreads across the US, in response to massive projects that have begun development and construction, frequently with little or no input from local residents. In Utah, [residents protested](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/933687/utah-stratos-project-data-center-kevin-oleary) after Box Elder County commissioners signed off on a data center expected to consume more than double …
